name: Nexus Theme Builder for Elementor
author: SmartWpThemes

sections.description:
Nexus Theme Builder for Elementor lets you build Elementor headers, footers, single templates, archives, search results, 404 pages, and reusable blocks with display conditions. Elementor is required; Elementor Pro is not required for the Free Theme Builder features.

The free plugin also includes a focused Elementor widget library and a dashboard where individual widgets can be enabled or disabled. WooCommerce-dependent widgets are registered only when WooCommerce is active.

An optional Pro extension is distributed separately and is not bundled or artificially locked inside this free WordPress.org package.

Free Theme Builder

The Free Theme Builder lets you design site templates with Elementor and control where each published template is used. Templates are created and managed from the Nexus Builder area in the WordPress admin.

Free template types

The Free edition supports the following template types:

  • Header — build a custom Elementor header and assign it to the entire site or selected locations.
  • Footer — build a custom Elementor footer and assign it globally or conditionally.
  • Single content templates — create Elementor layouts for posts and supported public custom post types.
  • Archive — design archive layouts for supported WordPress archive contexts.
  • Search Results Page — create an Elementor template for WordPress search-result pages.
  • 404 Page — replace the normal theme 404 output with an Elementor-designed template.
  • Custom Block — build reusable Elementor content that can be inserted where supported, including through the Nexus template shortcode.

The Theme Builder works with supported public post types and public taxonomies when they meet the plugin’s targetable-content requirements. This allows compatible third-party content types to participate without hard-coding every post type into the plugin.

Display conditions and template assignment

Every supported Theme Builder template can use assignment rules so a design appears only where it is intended.

Display Location

Display Location defines where a template is eligible to appear. Depending on the template type and available WordPress content, locations can include:

  • Entire site.
  • Singular content.
  • Posts and supported public post types.
  • Specific pages, posts, or supported custom content.
  • Front page.
  • Posts page.
  • Archives.
  • Author archives.
  • Date archives.
  • Public taxonomy archives and supported taxonomy terms.
  • Search results.
  • 404 context.

Exclude Location

Exclude Location creates exceptions to a broader Display Location rule. For example, a Header can target the entire site and exclude one landing page, or a Single template can target a post type while excluding selected content.

When a matching exclusion rule exists, the exclusion takes precedence over the matching display rule.

User Roles

Templates can also be restricted according to the current visitor. Supported choices include:

  • All users.
  • Logged-in users.
  • Logged-out visitors.
  • Individual WordPress roles available on the site.

This is useful for role-aware headers, account experiences, member areas, or layouts that should differ for signed-in and signed-out visitors.

Priority

Priority resolves situations where more than one published template matches the same visitor and location. When multiple eligible templates match, the template with the lowest Priority number wins.

This makes it possible to create a broad site-wide template and then create more specific templates that intentionally take precedence.

Custom Blocks and template shortcode

Published Nexus templates can be rendered through the template shortcode where shortcode output is appropriate:

[netb_template id="123"]

Replace 123 with the WordPress post ID of the published Nexus template you want to display.

Custom Blocks are useful for reusable sections, calls to action, information panels, promotional sections, or other Elementor-built content that should be maintained in one place and reused elsewhere.

Widget management

The Nexus Builder > Dashboard provides widget management for the Nexus widget library.

Free widgets can be enabled or disabled from the dashboard. A disabled widget is not registered with Elementor, helping site administrators keep the Elementor widget panel focused on the components they actually use.

Widget frontend assets are loaded according to the plugin’s widget/dependency logic rather than treating every optional feature as permanently active. WooCommerce-dependent widgets are registered only when WooCommerce is available.

Free Elementor widgets

The Free edition includes the following Elementor widgets.

1. Site Logo

Dynamically display your WordPress site logo anywhere.

2. Page Title

Display context-aware page and content titles dynamically.

3. Site Tagline

Dynamically display your configured WordPress site tagline.

4. Site Title

Dynamically display your WordPress site title.

5. Post Meta Info

Display contextual post metadata in Elementor layouts.

6. Breadcrumbs

Display contextual breadcrumb navigation for easier site exploration.

7. Copyright

Add customizable copyright information to footer layouts.

8. Reading Time Count

Display estimated reading time for posts and articles.

9. Search

Create customizable search with optional live results.

10. Counter

Display animated manual or dynamic numerical counters.

11. Info Card

Create attractive information, feature, and call-to-action cards.

12. Social Share

Add customizable social sharing buttons to your content.

13. Static/Dynamic Table

Create manual or dynamic data tables in Elementor.

14. Interactive Card

Create engaging interactive cards with visual effects.

15. Animated Heading

Create engaging headings with customizable animated text.

16. Logo Grid

Showcase logos in clean, responsive grid layouts.

17. Animated Link

Create stylish links with customizable hover animations.

18. Navbar

Build responsive navigation with branding, search, and actions.

19. Advanced Progress Bar

Display customizable progress bars with labels and values.

20. Post Grid

Display WordPress content in customizable responsive grids.

21. WooCommerce Categories

Display WooCommerce product categories in customizable layouts.

OPTIONAL EXTENDED / PRO EDITION

Nexus Theme Builder for Elementor Pro is a separate extension. It requires the Free plugin and extends the existing Nexus Builder architecture rather than replacing it.

The following information is provided so users can clearly understand what belongs to the optional extension. These Pro widgets and features are not included as locked executable functionality inside the Free WordPress.org package.

Pro Theme Builder extension

Mega Menu template type

When the Pro extension is active and its Mega Menu functionality is available, Pro registers the dedicated Mega Menu Theme Builder template type. This allows Elementor-built Mega Menu content to be maintained as a Nexus template and used by the Pro Mega Menu system without exposing a disabled premium template type in the Free edition.

Popup Builder template type

The Pro extension registers a dedicated Popup Builder template type. Popup layouts are designed with Elementor and reuse the existing Display Location, Exclude Location, and User Role assignment system. Pro adds page-load, delay, and exit-intent triggers together with visit-frequency controls for every visit, first visit, after a configured number of visits, or once per session.

Pro Elementor widgets

1. Advanced Button

Create customizable buttons with icons, badges, and effects.

2. Advanced Heading

Create advanced headings with highlights, decorations, and effects.

3. Advanced Icon Box

Create feature boxes with icons, images, and actions.

4. Advanced Image Gallery

Build customizable image galleries with advanced layouts and controls.

5. Cart

Display and customize WooCommerce cart information anywhere.

6. Charts

Visualize structured data using customizable chart layouts.

7. Comparison List

Create clear feature, service, or pricing comparisons.

8. Countdown Timer

Create customizable countdown timers for events and promotions.

9. Dynamic Content

Display dynamic WordPress content using flexible layouts.

10. FAQ

Create organized, interactive FAQ sections with flexible content.

11. Logo Carousel

Showcase logos using customizable responsive carousel layouts.

12. Mega Menu

Build advanced responsive menus with rich content support.

13. Offcanvas

Create flexible slide-in panels with dynamic content sources.

14. Post Gallery

Showcase WordPress content in image-focused gallery layouts.

15. Post List

Display WordPress content in flexible customizable lists.

16. Post / Custom Timeline

Display posts or custom content in chronological timelines.

17. Price Table

Create attractive pricing plans with features and actions.

18. Scrollnav

Create smooth section navigation for long Elementor pages.

19. Tabs

Organize manual or dynamic content into interactive tabs.

20. Testimonial

Showcase customer testimonials with ratings and reviewer details.

21. Vertical Menu

Build customizable vertical navigation with submenu support.

22. Video Player

Display customizable videos with flexible playback controls.

23. WooCommerce Products

Display WooCommerce products in flexible grids or carousels.

24. Changelog

Present product or project updates in structured layouts.

25. Image Masking

Create creative image presentations using customizable masking effects.

26. Custom Carousel

Create flexible carousels for custom slide-based content.

Pro WooCommerce Theme Builder widgets

When WooCommerce is active, Pro adds dedicated WooCommerce Single and Archive widget groups for Elementor-based product and shop/archive templates.

The WooCommerce Single group includes Breadcrumbs, Sale Badge, Product Title, Product Gallery, Product Price, Product Rating, Short Description, Add To Cart, Stock, Product Meta, Product Tabs, Description, Additional Information, Reviews, Upsells, Related Products, and Product Navigation.

The WooCommerce Archive group includes Breadcrumbs, Archive Title, Archive Description, Archive Products, Archive Categories, and Archive Filters. These work alongside the Pro Cart and WooCommerce Products widgets.

Pro extended Elementor features

In addition to Pro widgets, the extension adds supported Elementor-level visual features.

Background Image Parallax

Add smooth scroll-based motion to Elementor background images.

Animated Gradient Background

Create animated gradient backgrounds for Elementor elements.

Scroll Driven Motion

Add scroll-responsive motion and visual effects to elements.

Dynamic Text Highlight

Highlight selected text using creative customizable visual effects.

Free versus Pro summary

Free provides:

  • Theme Builder core.
  • Header and Footer templates.
  • Single-content templates.
  • Archive templates.
  • Search Results templates.
  • 404 templates.
  • Custom Blocks.
  • Display Location rules.
  • Exclude Location rules.
  • User-role/login-state targeting.
  • Template Priority.
  • Template shortcode reuse.
  • Widget enable/disable management.
  • 21 Free Elementor widgets.
  • WooCommerce Categories widget when WooCommerce is active.

Optional Pro adds:

  • Mega Menu Theme Builder template type and Mega Menu integration.
  • Popup Builder template type with Elementor-designed content, assignment rules, triggers, and visit-frequency controls.
  • Additional Pro Elementor widget library.
  • Advanced dynamic-content displays.
  • Advanced navigation widgets.
  • Additional post/list/gallery/timeline displays.
  • Pricing, comparison, FAQ, testimonial, chart and countdown widgets.
  • Advanced image, heading, icon-box, button, tab, video and carousel widgets.
  • WooCommerce Cart and Products widgets plus dedicated Single Product and Archive Theme Builder widget groups.
  • Background Image Parallax.
  • Animated Gradient Background.
  • Scroll Driven Motion.
  • Dynamic Text Highlight controls available in every Elementor widget Content tab.

Getting started with Nexus Builder

A typical workflow is:

  1. Decide what part of the site you want to design, such as a Header or Footer.
  2. Create the corresponding Nexus template.
  3. Assign a Display Location, for example Entire Site.
  4. Add exclusions if certain pages should retain another template.
  5. Choose User Roles only when visitor-based targeting is required.
  6. Use Priority to control which template wins when rules overlap.
  7. Open the template in Elementor.
  8. Add normal Elementor widgets and/or Nexus widgets.
  9. Publish the template.
  10. Test the relevant pages on desktop, tablet, and mobile.

For reusable content rather than a site-level Header/Footer/Single/Archive assignment, create a Custom Block and use it where supported, including with the [netb_template id="..."] shortcode.

External services

The Social Share widget can open third-party sharing services only after a visitor explicitly clicks the corresponding share button. The plugin does not contact these services on page load. Depending on the selected network, the service receives the current page URL and, where applicable, the page title or optional share text so it can compose the share.

  • Facebook — receives the page URL when the Facebook share action is clicked. Terms: https://www.facebook.com/legal/terms Privacy: https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy/
  • X — receives the page URL and optional share text when the X share action is clicked. Terms: https://x.com/en/tos Privacy: https://x.com/en/privacy
  • LinkedIn — receives the page URL when the LinkedIn share action is clicked. Terms: https://www.linkedin.com/legal/user-agreement Privacy: https://www.linkedin.com/legal/privacy-policy
  • Pinterest — receives the page URL and optional share text when the Pinterest share action is clicked. Terms: https://policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-of-service Privacy: https://policy.pinterest.com/en/privacy-policy
  • Reddit — receives the page URL and page title when the Reddit share action is clicked. Terms: https://redditinc.com/policies/user-agreement Privacy: https://redditinc.com/policies/privacy-policy
  • WhatsApp — receives the page URL and optional share text when the WhatsApp share action is clicked. Terms: https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/terms-of-service Privacy: https://www.whatsapp.com/privacy
  • Telegram — receives the page URL and optional share text when the Telegram share action is clicked. Terms: https://telegram.org/tos Privacy: https://telegram.org/privacy

The Email share action uses a local mailto: link and does not send data to a service selected by this plugin. The Native Share action uses the browser/operating system Web Share interface and sends the page URL/title/text only to the destination explicitly chosen by the visitor. The Copy Link action uses the browser clipboard locally. The Custom share action uses the URL template configured by the site administrator; any data handling by that destination is governed by the administrator’s chosen service.

The Static/Dynamic Table widget also has an optional administrator-configured CSV URL data source. When that source is enabled, the WordPress server sends an HTTP GET request to the URL entered by the site administrator so the CSV can be displayed. The request necessarily exposes the site’s server IP address and normal HTTP request metadata to that administrator-selected host. Because the destination is chosen by the site administrator rather than hard-coded by the plugin, its terms and privacy policy depend on the selected provider and should be reviewed by the site administrator before use.

Source code

All custom JavaScript and CSS shipped with this plugin is included in human-readable form inside the plugin package under assets/js/ and assets/css/. The plugin does not require a compilation or minification step to regenerate those distributed assets.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate Elementor.
  2. Install and activate Nexus Theme Builder for Elementor.
  3. Open Nexus Builder > Dashboard to review and enable the Free widgets you want available in Elementor.
  4. Create a new Nexus Theme Builder template.
  5. Select the appropriate Template Type, such as Header, Footer, Single, Archive, Search Results, 404, or Custom Block.
  6. Configure Display Location rules to determine where the template should appear.
  7. Add Exclude Location rules if the template needs exceptions.
  8. Configure User Roles when the template should be limited by login state or WordPress role.
  9. Set Priority when multiple templates may target the same location.
  10. Edit the template with Elementor, design the layout, and publish it.
  11. Visit a matching frontend location to confirm that the published template is being selected as intended.
sections.faq:
Does the Free Theme Builder require Elementor Pro?

No. Elementor is required, but Elementor Pro is not required for the Free Nexus Theme Builder workflow or any widget listed in the Free widget section.

Is the Pro functionality locked inside the Free plugin?

No. Nexus Theme Builder for Elementor Pro is a separately distributed extension. The Free plugin contains and provides the Free functionality described in this readme. Pro registers its own additional widgets and features when that separate extension is installed and active.

Can I build more than headers and footers?

Yes. The Free Theme Builder also supports supported single-content templates, archives, Search Results, 404 templates, and reusable Custom Blocks.

Can I target a template to a specific page or post?

Yes, when the content is available as a supported target. Use Display Location to include the required content and Exclude Location to create exceptions.

Which rule wins if a location is both included and excluded?

The matching exclusion takes precedence over a matching display rule.

Can templates change according to whether a user is logged in?

Yes. User Roles can target all users, logged-in users, logged-out visitors, or individual WordPress roles.

What happens if multiple published templates match?

The eligible matching template with the lowest Priority number wins.

Can I reuse a template through a shortcode?

Yes. Published Nexus templates can be rendered with [netb_template id="..."] where shortcode output is supported. Replace the placeholder with the required template ID.

Can I disable Nexus widgets I do not use?

Yes. Use the widget controls in Nexus Builder > Dashboard. Disabled Free widgets are not registered in Elementor.

Does WooCommerce have to be installed?

No. WooCommerce is required only for WooCommerce-dependent widgets. The rest of the Theme Builder and non-WooCommerce widget library can be used without WooCommerce.

What happens if WooCommerce is not active?

WooCommerce-dependent widgets are not made available, while the other Nexus widgets and Theme Builder functionality continue to work.

What happens if the optional Pro extension is deactivated?

The Free Theme Builder and Free widgets continue to work. Pages or templates that contain Pro-only widgets should be reviewed before deactivating Pro because those widgets are supplied by the separate Pro extension.

Is Mega Menu part of the Free plugin?

No. Mega Menu is provided by the optional Pro extension. The dedicated Mega Menu Theme Builder template type is registered by Pro when the relevant Pro functionality is available.

Can I use Nexus widgets on normal Elementor pages?

Yes. Widgets that are enabled and registered can be used in Elementor wherever their normal requirements are satisfied; they are not limited to Theme Builder templates.

Are compatible custom post types supported?

The Theme Builder and query-based widgets can work with supported public post types and taxonomies where the plugin exposes them as compatible targets or sources. Availability can depend on the individual widget/template context.

Can I use the Search widget for live search?

Yes. The Free Search widget includes an optional Live Search mode with a configurable minimum-character threshold.

Can the Counter use dynamic values?

Yes. In addition to manual numbers, the Counter includes supported count sources such as post/content counts, user-role counts, and comment counts, depending on the selected configuration.

Can the Table display WordPress content dynamically?

Yes. The Static/Dynamic Table supports manual table data and supported dynamic WordPress query configurations. It also contains bounded remote CSV data handling where that data source is selected.

Does the plugin send usage data or require an external account?

The Free Theme Builder does not require an external account to use its included functionality. External Demo or Upgrade links are administrator-initiated links rather than requirements for using the Free Theme Builder.
sections.changelog:
1.0.4.1.3

  • Added Popup Builder information to the Free Upgrade to Pro comparison.
  • Expanded the Free readme with current Pro upgrade information for Popup Builder and WooCommerce Single/Archive Theme Builder widgets.
  • Updated Free release and localization metadata for stable version 1.0.4.1.3.

1.0.4.1.2

  • Stability release for the Free plugin following the latest WordPress.org review audit.
  • Hardened Elementor template metadata updates so request-driven changes run only through the verified save flow with nonce and capability checks.
  • Improved late escaping for generated Elementor/widget HTML while preserving valid rendered markup.
  • Refined WordPress.org metadata and external-service URL declarations for a more reliable review and installation experience.
  • Final review-readiness cleanup: tightened remaining generated markup escaping and removed avoidable output-suppression cases without changing widget behavior.

1.0.4.1.1

  • Stabilized the 1.0.4.1 release with the latest Free widget and Dashboard refinements.
  • Improved WordPress.org review compliance for asset enqueueing, request sanitization, dependency metadata, readable JavaScript/CSS source assets, external-service disclosure, and translation packaging.
  • Hardened request-shape validation and narrowed Dashboard extension-setting payloads before dispatching extension save hooks.

1.0.4.1

  • Enhanced fixes for the Navbar widget.

1.0.4

  • Maintained the Free Theme Builder core and complete Free widget library.
  • Improved template assignment, Elementor editor integration, frontend rendering, localization, responsive behavior, security, and performance.
  • Updated WordPress.org submission metadata and separated extension-owned template functionality from the Free package.
  • Expanded readme documentation for the Free Theme Builder, Free widgets, and separately distributed Pro extension functionality.

1.0.3

  • Added translation files for supported languages.
  • Improved internationalization and escaping.

1.0.2

  • Added the plugin translation template.

1.0

  • Initial release.

  3. Assign a Display Location, for example Entire Site.
  4. Add exclusions if certain pages should retain another template.
  5. Choose User Roles only when visitor-based targeting is required.
  6. Use Priority to control which template wins when rules overlap.
  7. Open the template in Elementor.
  8. Add normal Elementor widgets and/or Nexus widgets.
  9. Publish the template.
  10. Test the relevant pages on desktop, tablet, and mobile.

For reusable content rather than a site-level Header/Footer/Single/Archive assignment, create a Custom Block and use it where supported, including with the [netb_template id="..."] shortcode.

External services

The Social Share widget can open third-party sharing services only after a visitor explicitly clicks the corresponding share button. The plugin does not contact these services on page load. Depending on the selected network, the service receives the current page URL and, where applicable, the page title or optional share text so it can compose the share.

  • Facebook — receives the page URL when the Facebook share action is clicked. Terms: https://www.facebook.com/legal/terms Privacy: https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy/
  • X — receives the page URL and optional share text when the X share action is clicked. Terms: https://x.com/en/tos Privacy: https://x.com/en/privacy
  • LinkedIn — receives the page URL when the LinkedIn share action is clicked. Terms: https://www.linkedin.com/legal/user-agreement Privacy: https://www.linkedin.com/legal/privacy-policy
  • Pinterest — receives the page URL and optional share text when the Pinterest share action is clicked. Terms: https://policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-of-service Privacy: https://policy.pinterest.com/en/privacy-policy
  • Reddit — receives the page URL and page title when the Reddit share action is clicked. Terms: https://redditinc.com/policies/user-agreement Privacy: https://redditinc.com/policies/privacy-policy
  • WhatsApp — receives the page URL and optional share text when the WhatsApp share action is clicked. Terms: https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/terms-of-service Privacy: https://www.whatsapp.com/privacy
  • Telegram — receives the page URL and optional share text when the Telegram share action is clicked. Terms: https://telegram.org/tos Privacy: https://telegram.org/privacy

The Email share action uses a local mailto: link and does not send data to a service selected by this plugin. The Native Share action uses the browser/operating system Web Share interface and sends the page URL/title/text only to the destination explicitly chosen by the visitor. The Copy Link action uses the browser clipboard locally. The Custom share action uses the URL template configured by the site administrator; any data handling by that destination is governed by the administrator’s chosen service.

The Static/Dynamic Table widget also has an optional administrator-configured CSV URL data source. When that source is enabled, the WordPress server sends an HTTP GET request to the URL entered by the site administrator so the CSV can be displayed. The request necessarily exposes the site’s server IP address and normal HTTP request metadata to that administrator-selected host. Because the destination is chosen by the site administrator rather than hard-coded by the plugin, its terms and privacy policy depend on the selected provider and should be reviewed by the site administrator before use.

Source code

All custom JavaScript and CSS shipped with this plugin is included in human-readable form inside the plugin package under assets/js/ and assets/css/. The plugin does not require a compilation or minification step to regenerate those distributed assets.
